# SMBAct MCP tools

14 tools. **app_only**: served only by the running app (and by `smbact-cli mcp serve` while it proxies to the app), not by a standalone `smbact-cli mcp serve`. **Switch**: the key in `mcp.json` → `settings.tools` (`smbact-cli mcp config tool.<name>=on|off`); no switch = always listed. Only `get_capabilities` and `get_version` work without a license.

| Tool | Title | read-only | destructive | idempotent | app_only | switch | license-free |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list_windows` | List windows | yes | no | yes | no | — | no |
| `list_displays` | List displays | yes | no | yes | no | — | no |
| `list_desktops` | List desktops | yes | no | yes | **yes** | — | no |
| `window_action` | Arrange a window | no | no | no | no | `window_action` | no |
| `focus_window` | Focus a window | no | no | yes | no | `focus_window` | no |
| `minimize_all` | Minimize all windows | no | no | yes | no | `minimize_all` | no |
| `move_window_to_desktop` | Move a window to a desktop | no | no | yes | **yes** | `move_window_to_desktop` | no |
| `close_window` | Close a window | no | **yes** | no | no | `close_window` | no |
| `get_capabilities` | What this server can do | yes | no | yes | no | — | yes |
| `get_version` | Version | yes | no | yes | no | — | yes |
| `get_window` | Get a window | yes | no | yes | no | — | no |
| `set_window_frame` | Move and resize a window | no | no | yes | no | `set_window_frame` | no |
| `move_window_to_display` | Move a window to a display | no | no | yes | no | `move_window_to_display` | no |
| `place_windows` | Place windows | no | no | yes | **yes** | `place_windows` | no |

Window fields (`list_windows` `fields`): `id`, `app`, `title`, `frame`, `display`, `minimized`, `fullscreen`, `maximized`, `desktop`, `on_current_desktop`, `active`, `black_listed`, `class`. Default: `id`, `app`, `title`, `frame`, `display`, `minimized`, `fullscreen`, `maximized`, `desktop`, `on_current_desktop`, `active`, `black_listed`. Only when known: `desktop`, `on_current_desktop`.

## list_windows

Lists the open application windows: id, app, title, frame (x, y, width, height in screen points, top-left origin), display index and state. Call it first to get the window_id the other tools need. Optional filters (class, display, include_minimized) and fields narrow it down; without them it lists every window.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | string | no | — | Only windows whose app name contains this text (case-insensitive). |
| `title` | string | no | — | Only windows whose title contains this text (case-insensitive). |
| `class` | string | no | — | Only windows whose class contains this text (case-insensitive): WM_CLASS on Linux, the window class on Windows, the app's bundle id or name on macOS. |
| `display` | integer (≥ 0) | no | — | Only windows on this display (the index list_displays reports). |
| `include_minimized` | boolean | no | `true` | false: leave minimized windows out. |
| `fields` | array of string (id, app, title, frame, display, minimized, fullscreen, maximized, desktop, on_current_desktop, active, black_listed, class) (items ≥ 1) | no | — | Return only these fields (id is always included). class is returned only when asked for; desktop and on_current_desktop (macOS) are returned by default when known. |

## list_displays

Lists the displays: index, frame, visible frame (without the menu bar and Dock) and which one is the main display.

No arguments.

## list_desktops

Lists the desktops (macOS Spaces) of every display: display index (as in list_displays), its desktops by number and which one is showing. list_windows gives each window's desktop. macOS only for now.

No arguments.

## window_action

Applies one SMBAct layout or state action to a window, exactly as the SMBAct hotkey would (on the display the window is on). Actions: left-half (left 1/2), right-half (right 1/2), top-half (top 1/2), bottom-half (bottom 1/2), center-half (middle 1/2, full height), first-third (left 1/3), center-third (middle 1/3), last-third (right 1/3), first-two-thirds (left 2/3), last-two-thirds (right 2/3), first-fourth (leftmost 1/4 column), second-fourth (2nd 1/4 column), third-fourth (3rd 1/4 column), last-fourth (rightmost 1/4 column), first-three-fourths (left 3/4), last-three-fourths (right 3/4), top-left (top-left quarter), top-right (top-right quarter), bottom-left (bottom-left quarter), bottom-right (bottom-right quarter), top-left-sixth (3x2 grid), top-center-sixth (3x2 grid), top-right-sixth (3x2 grid), bottom-left-sixth (3x2 grid), bottom-center-sixth (3x2 grid), bottom-right-sixth (3x2 grid), top-left-eighth (4x2 grid), top-second-eighth (4x2 grid), top-third-eighth (4x2 grid), top-right-eighth (4x2 grid), bottom-left-eighth (4x2 grid), bottom-second-eighth (4x2 grid), bottom-third-eighth (4x2 grid), bottom-right-eighth (4x2 grid), center (center, size kept), move-left (to the left edge, size kept), move-right (to the right edge, size kept), move-up (to the top edge, size kept), move-down (to the bottom edge, size kept), maximize (fill the display (toggles)), maximize-height (full height, width kept (toggles)), fullscreen (native fullscreen (toggles)), minimize (minimize), restore (back to the frame before the last SMBAct action), next-display (move to the next display), previous-display (move to the previous display). Returns the window frame before and after.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |
| `action` | `left-half` \\| `right-half` \\| `top-half` \\| `bottom-half` \\| `center-half` \\| `first-third` \\| `center-third` \\| `last-third` \\| `first-two-thirds` \\| `last-two-thirds` \\| `first-fourth` \\| `second-fourth` \\| `third-fourth` \\| `last-fourth` \\| `first-three-fourths` \\| `last-three-fourths` \\| `top-left` \\| `top-right` \\| `bottom-left` \\| `bottom-right` \\| `top-left-sixth` \\| `top-center-sixth` \\| `top-right-sixth` \\| `bottom-left-sixth` \\| `bottom-center-sixth` \\| `bottom-right-sixth` \\| `top-left-eighth` \\| `top-second-eighth` \\| `top-third-eighth` \\| `top-right-eighth` \\| `bottom-left-eighth` \\| `bottom-second-eighth` \\| `bottom-third-eighth` \\| `bottom-right-eighth` \\| `center` \\| `move-left` \\| `move-right` \\| `move-up` \\| `move-down` \\| `maximize` \\| `maximize-height` \\| `fullscreen` \\| `minimize` \\| `restore` \\| `next-display` \\| `previous-display` | yes | — | The action to apply. |

## focus_window

Brings a window to the front and focuses it (un-minimizes it if needed).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |

## minimize_all

Minimizes every window (except apps on the SMBAct black list): on all displays, only on the display of the active window, or only on the main display.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | `all` \\| `active` \\| `main` | no | `all` | all \| active \| main |

## move_window_to_desktop

Sends a window to another desktop (macOS Space) of its display, or of the display given by index. With follow = false the desktop you are on stays and the window disappears from it; with follow = true macOS switches to the target desktop and the window is focused there. Without follow: the user's SMBAct setting (Settings › Desktops, stay by default). A window in native full screen leaves full screen first, then moves (left_fullscreen in the result). Desktop numbers as in list_desktops. macOS only for now.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |
| `desktop` | integer (≥ 1) | yes | — | Desktop number (1 = the first desktop of that display). |
| `display` | integer (≥ 0) | no | — | Display index from list_displays; default: the window's display. |
| `follow` | boolean | no | — | true: go to the target desktop and focus the window there; false: stay on the current desktop. Default: the user's SMBAct setting (stay unless they chose "Go with the window"). |

## close_window

Closes a window, or every window of its application (scope "application"). Like clicking the close button: the app may ask to save. The user may have to confirm it in SMBAct.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |
| `scope` | `window` \\| `application` | no | `window` | — |

## get_capabilities

Describes this SMBAct server: app version, platform and coordinate space, whether tool calls are allowed (license) and why not, whether the window engine runs, which tools are switched on and which window_action actions this OS has. Works without a license.

No arguments.

## get_version

The SMBAct (or smbact-cli) version, build variant, platform and the MCP protocol versions. Works without a license.

No arguments.

## get_window

One window by its id (or "active"), with every field list_windows can return, class included.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |

## set_window_frame

Sets a window frame to exact coordinates: the visible frame, as list_windows reports it. Give any of x, y, width, height; the others stay as they are. Coordinates are the ones list_windows reports: screen points on macOS, physical pixels on Windows and Linux X11, logical pixels on GNOME and KDE Wayland, top-left origin (get_capabilities says which). A maximized, minimized or fullscreen window is brought back to normal first (state_changes). The app may limit the size: the result has the frame before, the one asked for and the actual one read back, and status / results as place_windows (this is place_windows with one placement and area "screen"). A frame that would leave no grabbable title bar on any display is refused (target_offscreen). window_action restore does not undo it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |
| `x` | integer (≥ -100000, ≤ 100000) | no | — | Left edge. |
| `y` | integer (≥ -100000, ≤ 100000) | no | — | Top edge. |
| `width` | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 100000) | no | — | — |
| `height` | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 100000) | no | — | — |

## move_window_to_display

Moves a window to another display the way next-display does: it keeps its place and size relative to the visible frame (a fullscreen or maximized window stays so). display is an index or a name from list_displays, or "main".

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `window_id` | string | yes | — | A window id from list_windows ("<pid>:<handle>"), or "active" for the frontmost window (usually your own MCP client). |
| `display` | integer/string | yes | — | The target display: its index (list_displays), its name, or "main". |

## place_windows

Puts one window or several at any geometry. Positions and sizes refer to the work area of the window's display by default (area "work": without menu bar, Dock, taskbar, panels): {"app": "Safari", "frame": "0,0,60%,100%"} is the left 60 %. For absolute coordinates as list_windows reports them use area "screen" (or set_window_frame). Coordinates are the ones list_windows reports: screen points on macOS, physical pixels on Windows and Linux X11, logical pixels on GNOME and KDE Wayland, top-left origin (get_capabilities says which). Lengths: integers (native units), "<n>dip", "<p>%", "<a>/<b>", "rel:<value>" (relative to the current frame; such a request is not idempotent). Also anchor / pivot, grid + cell, gap, margin, min_* / max_*, fit, display (an index, main, next, cursor, a name…). Targets: window_id (default "active", usually your own MCP client), or app, bundle_id, title, title_regex, pid, nth (front to back), with on_multiple, if_missing, wait_ms. Maximized, minimized and fullscreen windows are brought back to normal first (state "keep" refuses them). Placements run in order, best effort: the result has a status (applied, partial, failed, dry_run) and one row per window with before, requested, actual, delta, status (exact within tolerance, adjusted with reasons, unchanged, skipped, failed with an error). A partial result is not an error: read the rows. dry_run resolves without moving anything; simulate (with dry_run) uses given displays. get_capabilities.placement says what this OS supports.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `placements` | array of object (items ≥ 1, items ≤ 32) | yes | — | The placements, applied one after another in this order (1-32). |
| `strict` | boolean | no | `false` | A frame outside the tolerance counts as a failure (code constraint), not as adjusted. |
| `tolerance` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 64) | no | `1` | Native units a frame may be off and still count as exact. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `false` | Resolve and report (status would_place), move nothing. |
| `timeout_ms` | integer (≥ 500, ≤ 14000) | no | `10000` | The whole request; a placement still running then fails with timeout, the rest are not_attempted. |
| `simulate` | object | no | — | With dry_run only: resolve against these displays (and this window frame) instead of the real ones; no window is looked up. |
